en: When is the day that my pair of eyes shall rejoice, beholding
the dark Sapphire, the delicate One, who sleeps
— as clear-watered Poṉṉi rubs [His] feet
with the hands [that are her] waves —
in the great town of Śrīraṅgam
having reached
the bed of great whiteness shining with ornaments
called Ananta, the king of serpents, the great effulgence
whose forehead twinkles with gems that glow so that darkness retreats
[and] over whom spread a thousand hoods with groups of decorative spots?
When is the day that [I] will stand clutching the ‘Fragrance’ pillars [and]
praise to the satisfaction of my mouth
Māl who resembles a mountain that blooms with ironwood flowers
Māyōṉ who sleeps on the serpent-bed in the [well-]defended Raṅgam
[lying] beneath [the fire]
as the red fire
- which was spit [out] by the fiery serpent with a coiled body
[its] unique thousand mouths filled with verses of praise -
spreads everywhere so that it increases higher and higher
just like a canopy to [His] head that is [like] an unwithering blossom
When is the day that [I shall] approach that place, along with the servants
placing blossoms beneath the pair of feet of
the Lord, who sleeps on His serpent-bed in decorated Raṅgam
as his navel with the lotus flower appears
the red gold[-like] Lord who stood so that
Aja, who is in all ways honourable, pleasingly bows down
speaking highly of [Him], praising [Him] with all [of his] four tongues
worshipping [and] constantly praising [Him] with [his] eight graceful eyes
[that see in] all directions and with [his] four faces?
When is the day [I shall] join my hands in worship
strewing [freshly-]plucked blossoms
praising till [my] tongue is cleaved
Māl who ripped apart the horse’s jaw and rejoiced
the ocean-hued One, my Kṛṣṇa, the Bull among cowherds
who, that day, protected the cattle by holding up the mighty mountain
the Chief of the immortals
the pleasant Song in beautiful Tamil, the beautiful northern Language
the King who sleeps on the serpent-bed in Raṅgam
where those who have renounced attachment abide
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
those who have renounced all ties

en: On which day shall my head [bedecked with] flowers bow, having beheld
the sapphire-hued Lord who sleeps on the serpent-bed
in the prosperous, walled Raṅgam abounding in jewelled storied mansions and palaces
as the blissful Tumburu and Nārada fall [at His feet]
and praise [Him], practising the yāḻ [producing] sweet, peerless music
as Aja in the ancient lotus bows [and] praises [Him] incessantly
with the verses of praise [that are] the matchless ancient Vedas
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: When is the day that my heart shall greatly melt beholding
the lotus eyes and the radiant moon-like holy face of
the ocean-hued One, who sleeps having climbed upon the serpent
in Raṅgam, which has groves with blossoms [dripping] with honey
[and which,] Aja - on a lotus [sought by] bees -, Hara
a group of other immortals along with Indra, and Rambhā and the like
and moreover, a group of ascetics with clear minds
go to and reach, jostling [against each other] and strewing blossoms in all directions?
When is the day [I will] stand [there] as my eyes fill with tears, having seen
Māyōṉ of glowing lustre, who sleeps on the serpent-bed in Raṅgam
which Poṉṉi decorates, the Refuge of
those with hearts where dharma shines
who are servants who have stood steadfastly on the infinitely ancient path
ridding the mind of violence that it contains and curing [it of its] deceit
controlling the five senses, renouncing the affliction [caused by] the burden of trouble
[and] praising five times [a day]?
When is the day that I, with a forceful karma, will live
seeing and attaining the pleasure of union with
Mālōṉ, who sleeps on the serpent-bed
in Śrīraṅgam surrounded by groves [and] large paddy fields filled with carp
as the long Śārṅga abounding with arrows, the fine curved conch
the murderous discus, the cruel club, the sword glowing with victory [and]
the fierce victorious bird called Garuḍa, whose movement resembles the wind
— all these surround and guard [Him]?
When is the day [I shall] roll on the ground jumping [for joy] at seeing
the Lord with the belligerent discus, who sleeps on the serpent-bed in Śrīraṅgam
where the sound of the drum filled with excellence reminds [one] of the ocean everyday
[and] where throngs of servants, with inextinguishable love in [their] hearts
crowding [together] and singing many holy praises
melt thinking [of Him]
- so that a shower of tears, shed with an insatiable delight of heart, falls -
and extol [Him]?
When is the day I too shall fit in and stay with the big groups of servants who swell with joy
seeing [them] in the holy courtyard of Him of decorated Raṅgam
who sleeps facing the southern direction with love
so that the firm, great heavens are redeemed; so that the immortals are redeemed
so that the earth is redeemed; so that the humans of the earth are redeemed
so that the sorrow of exceeding affliction departs
so that happiness without any slackening grows
so that servants who rejoice at heart live?
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Those who master
all ten [songs] in the Tamil garland brilliant in rhythm
worded by the munificent Kulacēkaraṉ, king of the people of Kūṭal
—who shines with a [royal] parasol, a victorious army and a sword glowing with victory—
out of the desire to rejoice, having seen to the satisfaction of [his] eyes
the Lord with a dark-hued body that shines [like] the ocean
who sleeps on the serpent-bed in Śrīraṅgam
in the middle of the Poṉṉi with banks that shines with islets
shall reach below the feet of Nārāyaṇa shining with goodness
If [one] gets to see the throng of true servants who praise
the hard-to-seek, vigour[-giving] Honey, Him from Raṅgam in the South
Him with a chest [bedecked with] unwithering sylvan garlands
where Śrī lives
who, with [their] minds suffering from confusion
join the dance, get distressed, call [Him]
[and] attain forgetfulness
that is the purpose of eyes that [can] see
Wherefore the desire to bathe diving in the water of the Ganges
if we get to bathe in the dust of the feet of devotees who call [out] saying, ‘O Raṅga!’
singing and dancing, thinking only of these:
[His] embracing the pair of shoulders of the Woman of the lotus who is like a flower
[His] destroying the big trees that grew tall with a glowing arrow [and]
[His] grazing herds of cows?
I shall wear on my head the abundant slush from the red feet of the devotees
who make slush in the holy courtyard of Raṅga’s temple
with the tears of [their] eyes that stream like the mighty river of bounteous Poṉṉi
having sung, repeating
[His] killing the bulls, [His] splitting off the earth as a boar
[His] previously killing the enemies as Rāma, and [His] measuring the earth
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: My heart will applaud [by] praising the red feet of the devotees who
being the servants of
our Lord with arms that the cowherdess tied, being enraged at seeing
[Him] eat fresh, curdled curds, butter together with milk
my Raṅga
experience joy calling out, ‘Nārāyaṇa!’ so that [their] tongues become scarred
prostrate, so that [their] bodies are bruised, [and] extol [Him]
My heart will truly bristle [with joy] thinking of those who bristle [with joy]
as the King, who smashed the necks of the spurious bulls with roaring voices
and dragged the bellicose snake [out of the pond],—
He from Raṅgam in the South
surrounded by rock-made, solid, big ramparts glowing with radiance
the black Cloud with a bow [on Its] body—
reaches their hearts, [and] shines from [there]
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: My heart will love in all [my] births
the servants who love solely our Father Raṅga
wandering everywhere
showing the good path devoid of evil
so that the sinners
who are without the devotion [that consists in] bearing [on their heads]
the great lotus feet of the Lord of the celestial beings
who is the Beginning, the End, Infinity, a Marvel -
are redeemed
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: My heart will become [full of] love for the pair of feet of those who join [Him]
having the heart to join the one rare, great Light called Raṅga
Him with a pearl garland[-bedecked] chest, a red mouth
white teeth [like] good, shiny pearls [and]
a body resembling a cluster of clouds -
weep and stand with overflowing tears that trickle down
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Feeling love for
Him with lotus-eyes, Him with a mountain[-like] large, sacred chest
where a garland of fragrant sacred tulsi poked by bees dwells
Him who lay on the ocean that was agitated
rising, dancing, singing [and] wandering
the servants become mad solely on our Father, Raṅga -
My heart has felt desire for [their] happy lives
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, accusative
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: As the eyes exude tears that crowd together as [their] bodies bristle
pining, standing exhausted, growing weary, performing a worship dance
rising, dancing, singing, bowing [and] becoming the servants of
my Father, [my] Lord, Raṅga
they who are solely mad on Him are not madmen
[it is] the others who are complete madmen
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, dative

en: Those who master the sweet Tamil garland in the words of Kulacēkaraṉ
the guardian of Kolli, the master of Kūṭal, the king of Kōḻi
who has a heart that dwells forever in the state of limitless servitude of the true
servants of Raṅga, the Lord of the Woman on the big lotus blossom
shall become the servants’ servants
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: There will be no joining, for me
with this earth that takes unreal life to be real
I cry out saying, ‘O Master! O Raṅga!’
I have ended up bearing mad [love] for my own Māl
gloss: proper name, dative, third person, singular

en: There will be no associating, for me, with the world
that remains by the side of women with waists finer than thread
Dancing, calling out loud ‘O Raṅga!’
I have ended up with desire rising for my own Māl
There will be no associating, for me, with the people of [this] earth who pay homage
to the cruel striped bow of the venerable Kāma
[I am] the madman of Raṅga, Him with a pearl necklace on the chest, the Infinite One
the good Nārayaṇa, the Destroyer of hell
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: There will be no associating, for me, with this orb[-like earth]
that runs after food and clothes desiring [them]
See! I am the madman of the Him whose mouth sucked the breast of the mighty demoness
He of Raṅgam, He who resides in the [cosmic] egg
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, singular, masculine
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: There will be no associating, for me, with those whose law is doing otherwise
while there exists a good path with no vice
[I am] the madman of the Primal One, the Cowherd, Raṅga
the Husband of the woman Lakṣmī on the beautiful lotus
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, honorific, sociative
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: I shall not associate with those who do not belong to our Highest One
I shall not consider as worthy of regard the happy life of the celestials
[I am] the madman of our Lord, He of Raṅgam, the Lord of the immortals, for all seven births
The red-eyed Māl dispelled that intention to associate with anyone of any nature
I am calling out saying, ‘O Father! O Raṅga!’
I have ended up as a madman of our Lord
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: Everyone is a demon to me, and I too am a demon to everyone. Why speak of it?
I am calling out saying, ‘O Cowherd! O Raṅga!’
I have ended up becoming a demon of our Lord
There is no affliction here to those who master
the words uttered by Kulacēkaraṉ, the king of the Koṅku people
being a unique great madman whose mind remains on the pair of feet of
Raṅga with a discus in [His] beautiful hand
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: I will not desire birth in a body, the wealth of which [consists in having] flesh that builds up
but the state of servitude for Him who subdued the seven bulls
I shall be born as a heron living in the Kōṉēri [lake] in Veṅkaṭa
of Him who has a conch that is curved to [His] left
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: I shall not desire the wealth of ruling over the celestial world
with Rambhā and the like with unending wealth surrounding [me], nor an earthly kingdom
I shall possess the good fortune of being born
as a fish in the mountain spring of the sacred Veṅkaṭa with groves [full of] honey-filled flowers
[Going] along with [temple servants]
carrying the gold cup in which spits the King of Veṅkaṭa
who has a discus that glows [like] circular lightning
I shall get to enter
the lofty entrance of Vaikuṇṭha
which Indra, Brahmā and he with plaited matted locks, pushing [each other], [find] difficult to enter
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, imperfective aspect, first person, singular

en: I will possess the wealth of standing as a campaka-tree
in Veṅkaṭa, where the music-uttering swarms of bees hum the paṇ melody
for the sake of seeing the pair of [feet with] anklets of Māyōṉ
who sleeps inside the cool milk ocean which moves [and brings] radiant red corals to the shores
I shall not desire this kingdom or the happiness-abiding wealth
[that is] sitting upon the neck of an elephant in must that trembles
I shall possess the [fruit of] tapas [that enables me] to stand as a clump of grass
upon the mountain of the beautiful Veṅkaṭa of the Supreme Being, our Lord
The singing and the dancing of people like
Ūrvaśī and Menakā, women with lightning-like slender waists
- I shall not wish for those
I shall have the rare [fruit of] tapas of becoming such a golden mountain as Veṅkaṭa
in which swarms of bees hum the paṇ-melody saying ‘teṉṉa’
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: I shall not esteem the wealth of [being] celebrated being seated majestically
becoming the king of kings, under the white [royal] parasol
like the great full moon that reigns over the sky
I shall possess the design to flow as a jungle river
upon the mountain of the sacred Veṅkaṭa
with gardens [full of] flowers brimming with honey
I shall possess the state of lying as a path upon the mountain of the sacred Veṅkaṭa
with cool, fragrance-filled flower gardens
of Him who is the Vedas, Him who ends [their] grievances [as]
he with matted-locks on which the crescent moon stands
Brahmā and Indra [perform] big yajnas in the [proper] manner
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
participial noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: O Tirumāl who destroys forceful karmas that are evil!
O tall One! O You of Veṅkaṭa!
At the entrance of Your temple
I shall see Your red coral lips
lying as a step
on which devotees, celestial beings, Rambhā and the like dwell [and] walk about
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, vocative, third person

en: Even if, reigning over the celestial world under a single [royal] parasol
I get Ūrvaśī’s beautiful waist with a gold girdle
I will not wish for [them]
I will become anything on the golden mountain called the sacred Veṅkaṭa
of our Lord, He with red coral lips
Those who master the Tamil of [this] thread that was spun
- uttered by Kulacēkaraṉ with a sharp spear trained in killing
bowing down and desiring to see the gold-like red feet of Him of
Veṅkaṭa in the North with everlastingly cool mountain slopes—
are devotees agreeable [to Him] indeed
There is no refuge [for me] other than Your feet
[although You] do not curb the grief [that You] give [me]
O Lord of Viṟṟuvakkōṭu, surrounded by groves with blossoms mingled with fragrance!
Even though the mother who gave [him] birth casts [him] aside out of cutting anger
the infant cries thinking of her benevolence again
I have been like that
Like a woman of noble birth who does not know [anyone] but [her] husband
although [her] spouse does things that the beholders despise
O Lord of Viṟṟuvakkōṭu, surrounded by ramparts reaching the sky on [all] sides!
Even if You do not take possession of [and] accept me
I shall [still] speak of Your [feet with] roaring anklets
gloss: participial noun, third person, perfective aspect
participial noun, third person, neuter plural

en: O Lord of Viṟṟuvakkōṭu surrounded by vast paddy-fields, which the fish watch!
Even though You will not look in my direction
I have no attachment other than attachment for You
I have been like the subjects who live looking up to the sceptre of the garlanded king
whatever the grief he gives [them] by not looking after [them]
Like the sick man who [bears] undying affection for the physician
even though [he] cuts [him] with a knife [and] sears, O Lord of Viṟṟuvakkōṭu!
Even though through maya You give [me] suffering that does not disappear
I, who am [your] servant, shall look for the grace of You, who have not accepted [me]
O Lord of Viṟṟuvakkōṭu! O You who killed the robust male elephant with cruel eyes!
Where shall I go [and] be redeemed if not [by] reaching Your pair of feet?
I am like the great bird, which, going everywhere [but] not seeing the shore, [and]
returning to the surging ocean again, climbs the mast of the ship that meets [it]
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, second person, vocative

en: Even if the red fire itself comes [and] makes heat
the red lotus will not blossom except for the hot sun in the sky
Even if You do not destroy severe grief, O Lord of Viṟṟuvakkōṭu
I will not [have] my mind melt except for Your endless excellence
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, dative

en: For however long the clouds forget [them], the green shoots keep looking only
for the big clouds that rise turning black
Again, like them, I, who am [your] servant, will very much place my mind on You
O Lord of Viṟṟuvakkōṭu, even though You do not destroy [my] bodily sorrows
Again, like all those glistening rivers that join [together], spread, flow and
enter the ocean [that was] dug, unable to stay outside [of it]
O Lord of Viṟṟuvakkōṭu! O You of the colour of exceedingly shiny clouds!
I shall not enter [anything] other than Your gracefulness that shines entering [my heart]
see, O holy One!
Like the wealth that desires him who does not desire vast wealth
desiring [but] You [instead]
due to [Your] maya
O Lord of Viṟṟuvakkōṭu with a discus resembling lightning itself
I, who am [Your] servant, shall remain desiring only You
gloss: negative, participial noun, third person, masculine, singular

en: Those who master all ten [poems] in good Tamil
uttered by Kulacēkaraṉ with a victorious spear [and] army
who longed for His feet saying, ‘I do not have anyone else [as my] support
even though You do not want [me], O Lord of Viṟṟuvakkōṭu,’
shall not reach hell

ta: ஏர்மலர்ப் பூங்குழ லாயர்மாத ரெனைப்பல ருள்ளவிவ் வூரிலுன்றன்
மார்வு தழுவுதற் காசையின்மை யறிந்தறிந் தேயுன்றன் பொய்யைக்கேட்டுக்
வார்மணற் குன்றிற் புலரநின்றேன் வாசுதே வாவுன் வரவுபார்த்தே
en: Knowing of [my own] absence of desire for embracing Your chest
in this town where there are so many cowherd women
with curling hair [adorned with] beautiful, blooming flowers
despite knowing [it], listening to Your lie
I stood, as it dawned on the long sand bank on the river Yamunā
feeling the coolness of the abundant rain-like dew, getting shy, shivering
O Vāsudeva! expecting Your arrival

ta: கெண்டையொண் கண்மட வாளொருத்தி கீழை யகத்துத் தயிர்கடையக்
கண்டொல்லை நானுங் கடைவனென்று கள்ள விழியைவிழித் துப்புக்கு
வண்டமர் பூங்குழல் தாழ்ந்துலாவ வாண்முகம் வேர்ப்பச்செவ் வாய்துடிப்பத்
தண்டயிர் நீகடைந் திட்டவண்ணந் தாமோத ராமெய் யறிவனானே
en: Seeing an [innocent] woman with barbus[-like] shiny eyes churning curds in the eastern house
saying ‘I shall churn quickly,’ [You] eyed [her] with [Your] stealthy glance, and slipped in
As the curling-hair with flowers on which bees sit fell low and moved about
as the bright face perspired, as the red lips quivered:
the way You churned the cool curds, O Dāmodara, truly I know

ta: கருமலர்க் கூந்த லொருத்திதன்னைக் கடைக்கணித் தாங்கே யொருத்திதன்பால்
மருவி மனம்வைத்து மற்றொருத்திக் குரைத்தொரு பேதைக்குப் பொய்குறித்துப்
புரிகுழல் மங்கை யொருத்தி தன்னைப் புணர்தி யவளுக்கும் மெய்யனல்லை
மருதிறுத் தாயுன் வளர்த்தியூடே வளர்கின்ற தாலுன்றன் மாயைதானே
en: Giving a side-glance to one woman with long, dark tresses [bedecked with] flowers
thinking of a woman then, placing [Your] heart on [her]
speaking to another woman
intending lies for one simple-minded woman
embracing one woman with curly locks
You are not true to her either
O You who snapped asunder the arjun trees!
Your deceit does grow along with Your growth!
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, second person, singular, vocative

ta: தாய்முலைப் பாலி லமுதிருக்கத் தவழ்ந்து தளர்நடை யிட்டுச்சென்று
பேய்முலை வாய்வைத்து நஞ்சையுண்டு பித்தனென் றேபிற ரேசநின்றாய்
ஆய்மிகு காதலோ டியானிருப்ப யான்விட வந்தவென் தூதியோடே
நீமிகு போகத்தை நன்குகந்தா யதுவுமுன் கோரம்புக் கேற்குமன்றே
en: While there was nectar in the breast milk of the mother
crawling and walking with a tottering gait, You went [and]
placed [Your] mouth at the devil’s breast, sucked the poison
[and] stood for the others to rail [at You] calling [You] ‘a fool.’
While I am [here] with great, choice love, You well enjoyed great pleasure
with the female messenger who came [to You] as I had sent [her]
Does that too not befit Your wickedness?

ta: மின்னொத்த நுண்ணிடை யாளைக்கொண்டு வீங்கிருள் வாயென்றன் வீதியூடே
பொன்னொத்த வாடைகுக் கூடலிட்டுப் போகின்ற போதுநான் கண்டுநின்றேன்
கண்ணுற் றவளைநீ கண்ணாலிட்டுக் கைவிளிக் கின்றதுங் கண்டேநின்றேன்
என்னுக் கவளைவிட் டிங்குவந்தா யின்னமங் கேநட நம்பிநீயே
en: While in growing darkness [You] were going through my street
wearing a gold-like cloth veil, grasping a woman with a waist slender as lightning
I stood watching [You]
I also stood watching
your signalling with the eye and beckoning with a hand [gesture] a woman
You came upon by chance
Why did You come here leaving her [behind]? You go [back] there again, [O] Lord!

ta: மற்பொரு தோளுடை வாசுதேவா வல்வினை யேன்றுயில் கொண்டவாறே
யிற்றை யிரவிடை யேமத்தென்னை யின்னணை மேலிட்ட கன்றுநீபோய்
அற்றை யிரவுமோர் பிற்றைநாளு மரிவைய ரோடு மணைந்துவந்தாய்
எற்றுக்கு நீயென் மருங்கில்வந்தா யெம்பெரு மானீ யெழுந்தருளே
en: O Vāsudeva with shoulders that fought the wrestlers!
As [soon as] I, with forceful karma, fell asleep tonight, during the middle watch
You placed me in the plesant bed and went away
That night and the following day, You came embracing women
For what have You come by my side [now]? Our Lord! Be gracious [enough] to leave!

ta: பையர வின்னணைப் பள்ளியினாய் பண்டையோ மல்லோம்நாம் நீயுகக்கும்
மையரி யொண்கண்ணி னாருமல்லோம் வைகியென் சேரி வரவொழிநீ
செய்ய வுடையுந் திருமுகமுஞ் செங்கனி வாயுங் குழலுங்கண்டு
பொய்யொரு நாள்பட்ட தேயமையும் புள்ளுவம் பேசாதே போகுநம்பீ
en: O Sleeper on the bed that is the serpent with hoods!
We are not [our] old selves. Neither are we women -
with shining eyes [that have red] lines[and that are painted] with kohl
- whom You desire
You stop [Your] comings to our village after dawn
Enduring [Your] falsehood for one day
seeing the red clothes, the brilliant face, the red ripe fruit[-like] lips and curling hair
is enough
Do not speak falsehood. Go, Lord!
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative

ta: என்னை வருக வெனக்குறித்திட் டினமலர் முல்லையின் பந்தல்நீழல்
மன்னி யவளைப் புணரப்புக்கு மற்றென்னைக் கண்டுழ றாநெகிழ்ந்தாய்
பொன்னிற வாடையைக் கையிற்றாங்கிப் பொய்யச்சங் காட்டிநீ போதியேலும்
இன்னமென் கையகத் தீங்கொருநாள் வருதியே லெஞ்சினம் தீர்வன்நானே
en: Telling me, ‘May you come,’ You entered to embrace her
who stayed in the shadow of the pandal [made of] jasmine that blossoms in clusters
Afterwards, seeing me, becoming disturbed, You slipped off
Even though You left holding the gold-coloured garments in [Your] hand
showing false terror, I shall settle my score [with You]
if You again come within my grasp one day
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, feminine, accusative

ta: மங்கல நல்வன மாலைமார்வி லிலங்க மயிற்றழைப் பீலிசூடிப்
பொங்கிள வாடை யரையிற்சாத்திப் பூங்கொத்துக் காதிற் புணரப்பெய்து
கொங்கு நறுங்குழ லார்களோடு குழைந்து குழலினி தூதிவந்தாய்
எங்களுக் கேயொரு நாள்வந்தூத வுன்குழ லின்னிசை போதராதே
en: Wearing a feather from the peacock tail
putting on a bright, soft garment around the waist
placing flower bunches so that they are attached to the ears
as the auspicious, beautiful forest garland shone on [Your] chest
You came sweetly blowing the flute with the women with curly hair that smells of honey
embracing [them]
As You come blowing [the flute] one day, it is us that the music of Your flute will not reach
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, plural, sociative

ta: அல்லி மலர்த்திரு மங்கைக்கேள்வன் றன்னை நயந்திள வாய்ச்சிமார்கள்
எல்லிப் பொழுதினி லேமத்தூடி யெள்கி யுரைத்த வுரையதனைக்
கொல்லி நகர்க்கிறை கூடற்கோமான் குலசே கரனின் னிசையின்மேவிச்
சொல்லிய வின்றமிழ் மாலைபத்துஞ் சொல்லவல் லார்க்கில்லை துன்பந்தானே
en: There will be no affliction for those who are capable of uttering
all ten [songs of] the garland in sweet Tamil
that were uttered, joining [them] with sweet music
by Kulacēkaraṉ, the chief of the Kolli city, the emperor of Kūṭal
[who sang] the words spoken by the young cowherdesses desiring
the Husband of the woman Śrī who is on the lotus blossom
having disparaged [Him and] sulked during the middle watch of the night time

ta: ஆலை நீள்கரும் பன்னவன் றாலோ வம்பு யத்தடங் கண்ணினன்றாலோ
வேலை நீர்நிறத் தன்னவன் றாலோ வேழப் போதக மன்னவன் றாலோ
ஏல வார்குழ லென்மகன் றாலோ வென்றென் றுன்னையென் வாயிடை நிறையத்
தாலொ லித்திடுந் திருவினை யில்லாத் தாய ரிற்கடை யாயின தாயே
en: O [You who are] like a long sugarcane from the press, tālō!
O [You] with long, lotus eyes, tālō!
O [You] of a hue similar to the ocean water, tālō!
O [You who are] like an elphant calf, tālō!
O my Son with long, unguent[-perfumed] curling hair, tālō!
[I] have become the lowest among mothers
not having had the good karma to sing a lullaby to You
saying [this] again and again to the satisfaction of my mouth

ta: வடிக்கொ ளஞ்சன மெழுதுசெம் மலர்க்கண் மருவி மேலினி தொன்றினை நோக்கி
முடக்கிச் சேவடி மலர்ச்சிறு கருந்தாள் பொலியு நீர்முகிற் குழவியே போல
அடக்கி யாரச்செஞ் சிறுவிர லனைத்து மங்கை யோடணைந் தானையிற் கிடந்த
கிடக்கை கண்டிடப் பெற்றில னந்தோ கேச வாகெடு வேன்கெடு வேனே
en: I did not get to see
[Your] posture [as You] lay like an elephant, gazing sweetly at something above
placing [on it Your] red lotus eyes that are painted with kohl
[and] endowed with sharpness
bending the little dark feet with red lotus soles
joining with the palm of the hand all the little red fingers
having compressed [them] fully like a baby cloud shining with water
I am destroyed! I am destroyed! Alas! O Keśava!

ta: முந்தை நன்முறை யன்புடை மகளிர் முறைமு றைதந்தங் குறங்கிடை யிருத்தி
யெந்தை யேயென்தன் குலப்பெருஞ் சுடரே யெழுமு கிற்கணத் தெழில்கவ ரேறே
உந்தை யாவனென் றுரைப்பனின் செங்கேழ் விரலி னுங்கடைக் கண்ணினுங் காட்ட
நந்தன் பெற்றன னல்வினை யில்லா நங்கட் கோன்வசு தேவன்பெற் றிலனே
en: As the affectionate women who are good relations since former times
sat [You] on their respective laps taking turns and asked [You]
‘O my Father! O great Flame of our lineage!
O Bull who stole the beauty of a cluster of seven clouds! Who is Your father?’
Nanda got [that fortune], as [You] showed [him] with Your fingers of red hue and a side glance
Our king Vasudeva without good karma did not get [that chance]!
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

ta: களிநி லாவெழில் மதிபுரை முகமுங் கண்ண னேதிண்கை மார்வுந்திண் டோளும்
தளிர்ம லர்க்கருங் குழல்பிறை யதுவும் தடங்கொள் தாமரைக் கண்களும் பொலிந்த
விளமை யின்பத்தை யின்றென்றன் கண்ணாற் பருகு வேற்கிவள் தாயென நினைந்த
வளவிற் பிள்ளைமை யின்பத்தை யிழந்த பாவி யேனென தாவிநில் லாதே
en: O Kṛṣṇa!
The breath of me who am a sinner, who am now drinking with my own eyes
the joy of [Your] youth which shines
with a face like the beautiful full moon with delightful moonlight
strong shoulders, chest, and strong arms
that crescent moon[-like forehead underneath]
the black curly hair with blooming flowers, large lotus eyes
[but] who have lost the endless joy of [Your] childhood
which knows [nothing but] that ‘she is [my] mother’
shall not remain
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, third person, singular, dative
pronominalised noun, singular, genitive, first person

ta: மருவு நின்றிரு நெற்றியிற் சுட்டி யசைத ரமணி வாயிடை முத்தம்
தருத லுமுன்றன் தாதையைப் போலும் வடிவு கண்டுகொண் டுள்ளமுள் குளிர
விரலைச் செஞ்சிறு வாயிடைச் சேர்த்து வெகுளி யாய்நின்று ரைக்குமவ் வுரையுந்
திருவி லேனொன் றும்பெற்றிலே னெல்லாந் தெய்வ நங்கை யசோதைபெற் றாளே
en: I, who am unfortunate, did not get anything; the divine lady Yaśodā got [it] all
[Your] giving a kiss with the gem[-like] mouth
as the cuṭṭi joined on the forehead moves about
and those words [You] stood uttering becoming angry
joining the little red fingers to the mouth
— so that the heart feels refreshed inside at
recognizing the beauty that is similar to Your father’s
gloss: pronominalised noun, negative, first person, singular

ta: தண்ணந் தாமரைக் கண்ணனே கண்ணா தவழ்ந்தெ ழுந்து தளர்ந்ததோர் நடையால்
மண்ணிற் செம்பொடி யாடிவந் தென்றன் மார்வில் மன்னிடப் பெற்றிலே னந்தோ
வண்ணச் செஞ்சிறு கைவிர லனைத்தும் வாரி வாய்க்கொண்ட வடிசிலின் மிச்சில்
உண்ணப் பெற்றிலே னோகொடு வினையே னென்னை யென்செய்யப் பெற்றதெம் மோயே
en: O Kṛṣṇa! O You with cool, beautiful lotus eyes!
I did not get to [have You] crawl, rise, come [to me] with a staggering walk and stay on my breast
having played with the red dust of the soil! Alas!
I did not get to eat the leftover of the boiled rice
which [You] scooped with all the beautiful little red fingers [and] placed [in Your] mouth
O! What [ever] did the mother of me with cruel karma, beget [me] for?

ta: குழ கனேயென்தன் கோமளப் பிள்ளாய் கோவிந் தாவென் குடங்கையின் மன்னி
ஒழுகு பேரெழி லிளஞ்சிறு தளிர்போ லொருகை யாலொரு முலைமுக நெருடா
மழலை மென்னகை யிடையிடை யருளா வாயி லேமுலை யிருக்கவென் முகத்தே
எழில்கொள் நின்றிருக் கண்ணிணை நோக்கந் தன்னை யுமிழந் தேனிழந் தேனே
en: O Beautiful One! O my delicate Son! O Govinda!
I have lost, I have lost the gaze of Your beautiful pair of sacred eyes on my face
as, staying in my palms, [You] rub gently the tip of one breast with the hand
that resembles a young, small tender shoot flowing with great beauty
[and] bestow from time to time the gentle smile of an infant, as [my other] breast is in [Your] mouth

ta: முழுதும் வெண்ணெ யளைந்துதொட் டுண்ணும் முகிழி ளஞ்சிறுத் தாமரைக் கையும்
எழில்கொள் தாம்புகொண் டடிப்பதற் கெள்கு நிலையும் வெண்தயிர் தோய்ந்தசெவ் வாயும்
அழுகை யுமஞ்சி நோக்குமன் னோக்கு மணிகொள் செஞ்சிறு வாய்நெளிப் பதுவும்
தொழுகை யுமிவை கண்ட வசோதை தொல்லை யின்பத் திறுதிகண் டாளே
en: Yaśodā who saw these
[Your] little tender budding lotus[-like] hands that take hold of and eat the butter
having wholly mixed [it] up
the state of fear at [her] striking [You] with the beautiful cord
[Your] red mouth filled with white curds
[Your] crying
that glance given fearing [her]
[Your] twisting [Your] beautiful, small, red lips
and [Your] worshipping [gesture] -
saw the bounds of great happiness

ta: குன்றி னாற்குடை கவித்ததுங் கோலக் குரவை கோத்த துங்குட மாட்டும்
கன்றி னால்விள வெறிந்ததுங் காலாற் காளி யன்றலை மிதித்ததும் முதலா
வென்றி சேர்பிள்ளை நல்விளை யாட்ட மனைத்தி லுமங்கென் னுள்ளமுள் குளிர
ஒன்றுங் கண்டிடப் பெற்றிலே னடியேன் காணு மாறினி யுண்டெனி லருளே
en: I, who am a servant, did not get to see anything [being] there
so that my heart feels refreshed inside:
none of the children’s good games endowed with victory starting from
[Your] spreading an umbrella with the hill
[Your] performing the beautiful kuravai-dance and the dance with waterpots
[Your] smashing the wood-apple tree with a calf
and [Your] treading on Kāliya’s head with the feet!
If there is a means for me [who am a servant], to see [all that], [do] bestow [it upon me]
gloss: verbal noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect

ta: வஞ்ச மேவிய நெஞ்சுடைப் பேய்ச்சி வரண்டு நார்நரம் பெழக்கரிந் துக்க
நஞ்ச மார்தரு சுழிமுலை யந்தோ சுவைத்து நீயருள் செய்து வளர்ந்தாய்
கஞ்ச னாள்கவர் கருமுகி லெந்தாய் கடைப்பட் டேன்வெறி தேமுலை சுமந்து
தஞ்ச மேலொன்றி லேனுய்ந்திரு ந்தேன் றக்க தேநல்ல தாயைப்பெற் றாயே
en: Alas! You grew up bestowing grace [by] tasting the guileful poison-filled breast
that the demoness possessing a heart in which deceit dwelt gave [to You]
so that [she], having been dried out
[her] sinews and nerves came out, [and] were charred and scattered
O my dark cloud[-like] Father, who robbed Kaṃsa [of his] days!
I have become the lowest, bearing breasts uselessly
I, who have no better refuge, have merely subsisted [for You]
You have indeed obtained a suitably good mother!

ta: மல்லை மாநகர்க் கிறையவன் றன்னை வான்செ லுத்திவந் தீங்ஙன மாயத்
தெல்லை யிற்பிள்ளை செய்வன காணாத் தெய்வத் தேவகி புலம்பிய புலம்பல்
கொல்லி காவலன் மாலடி முடிமேற் கோல மாங்குல சேகரன் சொன்ன
நல்லி சைத்தமிழ் மாலைவல் லார்கள் நண்ணு வாரொல்லை நாரண னுலகே
en: Those who master the good musical Tamil garland—
by Kulacēkaraṉ, the guardian of Kolli, whose crown of the head is embellished by Māl’s feet
who uttered the lament cried out by
the divine Devakī, who did not see the deeds of limitless maya of
[her] Son, who came [to her] thus
having dispatched to heaven the chief of the great, rich city
—shall rapidly reach Nārayaṇa’s world itself
O You who flourished in the gem [of a] womb of Kauśālyā of enduring glory!
O You who made the heads of the king of Lankā in the South to be strewn!
O Apple of my eye from Kaṇapuram made of red gold
surrounded on [all] sides by good, big, imperishable ramparts!
O My sweet Nectar! O Rāghava! Tālēlō!
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
causative, perfective aspect, participial noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: O You who created the whole earth on that lotus blossom!
You who bent the bow for piercing the bosom of Tāḍakā of robust vigour!
O Apple of my eye from Kaṇapuram [seeing whom] the beholders offer their hearts!
O You to whom all eight directions are subservient! O Rāghava! Tālēlō!
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, feminine, singular
perfective aspect, participial noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: O You who are the Support of the lineage of Kauśālyā of dark-coloured curls full of fragrance!
O Son of Daśaratha! O sacred Son-in-law of Janaka of great, everlasting fame!
O Apple of my eye from Kaṇapuram rich in [watercourses] purer than the Ganges!
O sweet Nectar of our lineage! O Rāghava! Tālēlō!
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: O You who created that Brahmā on the lotus!
O Daśaratha’s great Son! O Maithilī’s Husband!
O Apple of my eye from Kaṇapuram, where swarms of bees hum the kāmaram music!
O You who are capable [of mastering] the bow combined with arrows! O Rāghava! Tālēlō!
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative

en: Bestowing the expansive wealth of reigning over the earth on the noble Bharata himself
O You, who reached the difficult forest with the younger brother
[who bears You] love that is not satiated!
O You with a mountain[-like] chest reigned by excellence!
O King of Tirukaṇṇapuram! O my Dāśarathi with long hair reigned by a garland, tālēlō!
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, vocative, third person

en: O You who reached the ancient forest as all the kinsmen followed behind!
O rare Remedy to the renouncers! O King of the city of Ayodhyā!
O Apple of my eye from Kaṇapuram, where the learned people live!
O Śrīrāma, who accepted the younger stepmother’s word! Tālēlō!

en: O You who swallowed the world that day as an infant on a banyan leaf!
O You who, having killed Vālin, gave [his] kingdom to the young monkey!
O Apple of my eye from Kaṇapuram, where due to the wind, pearls dash against the shores!
O king of the town of Āli! O King of Ayodhyā, tālēlō!

participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine, singular, vocative

en: Building a bridge with hills, O You who destroyed the fortressed Laṅkā!
Churning the wavy sea, O You who bestowed nectar upon the immortals!
O Apple of my eye from Kaṇapuram where exponents in arts live!
O capable Archer! O Warrior! O Śrīrāma, tālēlō!

perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative

en: O Support of the lineage of Daśaratha
with fragrant tufts of hair, the fastening of which becomes loosened!
O You who destroyed the fortressed Laṅkā with a unique bow, for [it] to bend!
O Apple of my eye from Kaṇapuram
where the purple waterlilies that were weeded out blossom on the side!
O Rāghava who has grace for the younger brothers! Tālēlō!
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative
participial noun, singular, vocative, second person

en: O You who created the devas, the asuras and the directions!
O You who slept in the town of Raṅgam so that everyone comes [and] worships [Your] feet!
O Apple of my eye from Kaṇapuram where the good river Kāvēri flows!
O Rāghava, capable [Wielder] of the cruel, striped bow [fitted] with arrows! Tālēlō!
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: Those who master all ten [verses] of
the thread that is spun, the Tamil garland which said ‘tālēlō’ to the feet of
my Kākutstha from Kaṇapuram that imperishable, good, big ramparts surround on [all] sides
uttered by Kulacēkaraṉ with the [royal] parasol
the capable [wielder] of the spear trained in killing
are devotees agreeable [to Him]

ta: வன்றாளி னிணைவணங்கி வளநகரந் தொழுதேத்த மன்ன னாவான்
நின்றாயை யரியணைமே லிருந்தாயை நெடுங்கானம் படரப் போகு
வென்றாளெம் மிராமாவோ வுனைப்பயந்த கைகேசி தன்சொற் கேட்டு
நன்றாக நானிலத்தை யாள்வித்தேன் நன்மகனே யுன்னை நானே
en: My good Son!
Well did I have You reign over the earth, listening to the words of Kaikeyī who begot You
O my Rāma! She said, ‘Go [and] reach the vast forest’ to
You who sat on the throne [and] stood to become king
as the wealthy city paid homage to [and] praised [You]
worshipping [Your] pair of mighty feet!
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, second person, singular, accusative
perfective aspect, participial noun, second person, singular, accusative
causative, perfective aspect, first person, singular

ta: வெவ்வாயேன் வெவ்வுரைகேட் டிருநிலத்தை வேண்டாதே விரைந்து வென்றி
மைவாய களிறொழிந்து தேரொழிந்து மாவொழிந்து வனமே மேவி
நெய்வாய வேல்நெடுங்கண் ணேரிழையு மிளங்கோவும் பின்பு போக
எவ்வாறு நடந்தனையெம் மிராமாவோ வெம்பெருமா னென்செய் கேனே
en: O our Lord, O our Rāma! What shall I do?
Having listened to the cruel words of me with a cruel mouth
not desiring the vast earth, making haste
leaving off the horses, leaving off the chariot
leaving off the victorious, black-mouthed male elephant
[and] reaching the forest, how [ever] did You walk
as She with fine jewels [and] with eyes long as spears with oiled tips and the prince went behind [You]?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, neuter plural

ta: கொல்லணைவேல் வரிநெடுங்கட் கௌசலைதன் குலமதலாய் குனிவில் லேந்தும்
மல்லணைந்த வரைத்தோளா வல்வினையேன் மனமுருக்கும் வகையே கற்றாய்
மெல்லணைமேல் முன்துயின்றா யின்றினிப்போய் வியன்கான மரத்தி னீழல்
கல்லணைமேற் கண்டுயிலக் கற்றனையோ காகுத்தா கரிய கோவே
en: O Support of the lineage of Kauśālyā
with long, streaked eyes [like] spears that have embraced killing!
O You with mountain[-like] shoulders endowed with strength that hold up a bent bow!
You have learnt the means to melt the heart of me with forceful karma!
Have You, who had previously slept on soft beds, learnt to sleep on a stone bed
under the shade of the trees of the vast forest from now onwards, going [there] today?
O Kākutstha! O dark King!
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative
pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative
participial noun, perfective aspect, second person, singular

ta: வாபோகு வாயின்னம் வந்தொருகால் கண்டுபோ மலராள் கூந்தல்
வேய்போலு மெழிற்தோளி தன்பொருட்டா விடையோன்றன் வில்லைச் செற்றாய்
மாபோகு நெடுங்கானம் வல்வினையேன் மனமுருக்கும் மகனே யின்று
நீபோக வென்னெஞ்ச மிருபிளவாய்ப் போகாதே நிற்கு மாறே
en: Come, go, come again, come and see me once and leave
O You who destroyed the bow of him on the bull for the sake of Her
with graceful shoulders like bamboos [and] long tresses ruled by blossoms!
[O] the nature of my heart that remains steadfast without becoming split into two as
You go today, O Son, who melts the heart of me with forceful karma
to the boundless forest where elephants wander

ta: பொருந்தார்கை வேல்நுதிபோற் பரற்பாய மெல்லடிகள் குருதி சோர
விரும்பாத கான்விரும்பி வெயிலுறைப்ப வெம்பசிநோய் கூர வின்று
பெரும்பாவி யேன்மகனே போகின்றாய் கேகயர்கோன் மகளாய்ப் பெற்ற
வரும்பாவி சொற்கேட்ட வருவினையே னென்செய்கே னந்தோ யானே
en: O Son of me, who am a great sinner! You are going today
so that [Your] soft feet exude blood
as the stones pierce like the tips of spears in the hands of the enemies
desiring the undesirable jungle
so that the heat and the glare of the sun burn
so that the cruel pain of hunger is excessive!
What shall I do
[I] who have uncommon karma
who listened to the words of the hardened sinner
whom the king of Kēkayas begot as a daughter? Alas!

ta: அம்மாவென் றுகந்தழைக்கு மார்வச்சொற் கேளாதே யணிசேர் மார்வம்
என்மார்வத் திடையழுந்தத் தழுவாதே முழுசாதே மோவா துச்சிக்
கைம்மாவின் னடையன்ன மென்னடையுங் கமலம்போல் முகமுங் காணாது
எம்மானை யென்மகனை யிழந்திட்ட விழித்தகையே னிருக்கின் றேனே
en: I, who am of an inferior character, [still] live
[I] who have lost our Lord, my Son
[even] without hearing the affectionate word of [His] rejoicingly calling [me] ‘Father!’
without embracing [Him] so that His bejewelled chest is pressed against my chest
without having been close [with Him]
without smelling the crown of [His] head
without seeing [His] gentle gait [that is] like the gait of an elephant
[and His] lotus-like face

ta: பூமருவு நறுங்குஞ்சி புன்சடையாய்ப் புனைந்துபூந் துகில்சே ரல்குல்
காமரெழில் விழலுடுத்துக் கலனணியா தங்கங்க ளழகு மாறி
யேமருதோ ளென்புதல்வன் யானின்று செலத்தக்க வனந்தான் சேர்தல்
தூமறையீ ரிதுதகவோ சுமந்திரனே வசிட்டனே சொல்லீர் நீரே
en: You tell [me], O Vasiṣṭha! O Sumantra! Is it appropriate, O holy brahmins
that my Son, who has [such] arms that [the foes] are perplexed
should reach the forest that I am fit to go to today
wearing [His] scented tufts of hair bedecked with flowers in
matted locks that are tawny
putting on the desirably beautiful darbha-grass around [His] loins
that [usually] sports gold clothes
the beauty of [His] limbs having changed [with His] not wearing ornaments?
gloss: pronominalised noun, second person, plural, vocative

ta: பொன்பெற்றா ரெழில்வேதப் புதல்வனையுந் தம்பியையும் பூவை போலும்
இன்பற்றா நுண்மருங்குல் மெல்லியலென் மருகியையும் வனத்திற் போக்கி
நின்பற்றா நின்மகன்மேற் பழிவிளைத்திட் டென்னையுநீள் வானிற் போக்க
என்பெற்றாய் கைகேசீ யிருநிலத்தி லினிதாக விருக்கின் றாயே
en: O Kaikeyī, what did you get by sending to the forest
[my] Son who [learnt] the graceful Vedas from those who bear excellence
[His] younger brother, and my pūvai-flower-like Daughter-in-law of delicate build
who has a slender waist, which [even] the lightning cannot compare with
by creating blame on your son who you are attached to, and
by sending me too to high heaven?
You live happily on this vast earth!

ta: முன்னொருநாள் மழுவாளி சிலைவாங்கி யவன்றவத்தை முற்றுஞ் செற்றாய்
உன்னையுமுன் னருமையையு முன்மோயின் வருத்தமுமொன் றாகக் கொள்ளா
தென்னையுமென் மெய்யுரையு மெய்யாகக் கொண்டுவனம் புக்க வெந்தாய்
நின்னையே மகனாகப் பெறப்பெறுவே னேழ்பிறப்பு நெடுந்தோள் வேந்தே
en: O You who, having once obtained the bow from the axe-wielder
completely destroyed that one’s tapas
O my Father who entered the forest taking me and my promise to be the truth
without considering as worthy of regard Yourself
or the difficulty [we had in] obtaining You or Your mother’s suffering!
O long-armed King! I shall get to beget Yourself as [my] son for all seven births [to come]!

ta: தேனகுமா மலர்க்கூந்தற் கௌசலையுஞ் சுமித்திரையுஞ் சிந்தை நோவக்
கூனுருவில் கொடுந்தொழுத்தை சொற்கேட்ட கொடியவள்தன் சொற்கொண் டின்று
கானகமே மிகவிரும்பி நீதுறந்த வளநகரைத் துறந்து நானும்
வானகமே மிகவிரும்பிப் போகின்றேன் மனுகுலத்தார் தங்கள் கோவே
en: I am going to heaven, greatly desiring [it], also renouncing the wealthy city
which You renounced today greatly desiring the forest
accepting the words of the cruel woman
who listened to the words of the maidservant as crooked as [her] hunchbacked form
so that Sumitrā and Kausalyā
—with long tresses with big, blooming flowers [brimming] with honey—
are aggrieved in their minds
O King of the people of Manu’s lineage!
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, feminine, singular

ta: ஏரார்ந்த கருநெடுமா லிராமனாய் வனம்புக்க வதனுக் காற்றா
தாரார்ந்த தடவரைத்தோள் டயரதன்றான் புலம்பியவப் புலம்பல் தன்னைக்
கூரார்ந்த வேல்வலவன் கோழியர்கோன் குடைக்குலசே கரன்சொற் செய்த
சீரார்ந்த தமிழ்மாலை யிவைவல்லார் தீநெறிக்கட் செல்லார் தாமே
en: Those who master
these Tamil garlands filled with excellence, that lament
- which Daśaratha, with large mountain[-like] shoulders bedecked with garlands
[uttered] lamentingly
as the dark tall Māl full of beauty [born] as Rāma entered the forest
being unconsolable about that -
put into words by Kulacēkaraṉ [who has] a [royal] parasol
the king of the Kōḻi people, capable [wielder of] a lance that is full of sharpness
shall not go in the evil path
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular

ta: அங்கணெடு மதிட்புடைசூ ழயோத்தியென்னு மணிநகரத் துலகனைத்தும் விளக்குஞ் சோதி
வெங்கதிரோன் குலத்துக்கோர் விளக்காய்த் தோன்றி விண்முழுது முயக்கொண்ட வீரன்றன்னைச்
செங்கணெடுங் கருமுகிலை யிராமன் றன்னைத் தில்லைநகர்த் திருச்சித்ர கூடந் தன்னுள்
ளெங்கள்தனி முதல்வனையெம் பெருமான் றன்னை யென்றுகொலோ கண்குளிரக் காணு நாளே
en: When is the day [I shall] see, so that [my] eyes are refreshed
our Lord, our sole First Cause inside Tiruccitrakūṭam in the town of Tillai
Rāma, the tall dark-hued Cloud with red eyes
the Warrior who redeemed the whole of heaven
by appearing as a light to the lineage of the glowing Sun
the Flame that brightens all the worlds in the decorated city called Ayodhyā
surrounded by beautiful places and tall fortifications on [all] sides
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, masculine, accusative, third person, singular

ta: வந்தெதிர்ந்த தாடகைதன் னுரத்தைக் கீறி வருகுருதி பொழிதர வன்கணையொன் றேவி
மந்திரங்கொள் மறைமுனிவன் வேள்வி காத்து வல்லரக்க ருயிருண்ட மைந்தன் காண்மின்
செந்தளிர்வாய் மலர்நகைசேர் செழுந்தண் சோலைத் தில்லைநகர்த் திருச்சித்ர கூடந் தன்னுள்
ளந்தணர்க ளொருமூவா யிரவ ரேத்த வணிமணியா சனத்திருந்த வம்மான் றானே
en: See the young Man who consumed the lives of the mighty rakshasas
having saved the yajna of the Veda[-knowing] sage who possessed mantras
[by] discharging a unique, powerful arrow so that
[as it] sliced the chest of Tāḍakā who came and confronted [Him]
[her] oozing blood overflowed
[He is] the Father Himself
who rested on the decorated, bejewelled throne as the three thousand unique brahmins praised
inside Tiruccitrakūṭam, in the town of Tillai with fertile, cool gardens
[teeming] with flowers blooming among red shoots

ta: செவ்வரிநற் கருநெடுங்கட் சீதைக் காகிச் சினவிடையோன் சிலையிறுத்து மழுவா ளேந்தி
வெவ்வரிநற் சிலைவாங்கி வென்றி கொண்டு வேல்வேந்தர் பகைதடிந்த வீரன் றன்னை
தெவ்வரஞ்ச நெடும்புரிசை யுயர்ந்த பாங்கர்த் தில்லைநகர்த் திருச்சித்ர கூடந் தன்னுள்
ளெவ்வரிவெஞ் சிலைத்தடக்கை யிராமன் றன்னை யிறைஞ்சுவா ரிணையடியே யிறைஞ்சி னேனே
en: I have bowed down before the pair of feet of those who bowed down
to Rāma with broad arms [and] a cruel bow that is difficult to discharge
inside Tiruccitrakūṭam, in the town of Tillai with tall places and
[such] high walls that the enemies are afraid
to the Warrior who snapped asunder the bow of the angry one on the bull
for the sake of Sītā with excellent eyes that are red-streaked
dark-coloured [and] long
obtained the cruel, striped, good bow of the carrier of the axe weapon
and reduced the enemy of the speared kings by gaining victory [over him]

ta: தொத்தலர்பூஞ் சுரிகுழற்கை கேசி சொல்லால் தொன்னகரந் துறந்துதுறைக் கங்கை தன்னைப்
பத்தியுடைக் குகன்கடத்த வனம்போய்ப் புக்குப் பரதனுக்குப் பாதுகமு மரசு மீந்து
சித்திரகூ டத்திருந்தான் றன்னை யின்று தில்லைநகர்த் திருச்சித்ர கூடந் தன்னுள்
ளெத்தனையுங் கண்குளிரக் காணப் பெற்ற விருநிலத்தார்க் கிமையவர்நே ரொவ்வார் தாமே
en: The unblinking-ones themselves shall not be equal in comparison
with the inhabitants of [this] vast world who got to see [Him] even a little, today
so that [their] eyes are much refreshed, inside Tiruccitrakūṭam in the town of Tillai
Him who sat in Citrakūṭa
having abandoned the ancient city because of the words of Kaikeyī
with curly hair [adorned with] flowers blossoming in clusters
reached and entered the forest
as Guha, who bears devotion, took [Him] across the river Ganges
[and] given the sandals and the kingdom to Bharata
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect
pronominalised noun, third person, plural, dative

ta: வலிவணக்கு வரைநெடுந்தோள் விராதைக் கொன்று வண்டமிழ்மா முனிகொடுத்த வரிவில் வாங்கி
கலைவணக்கு நோக்கரக்கி மூக்கை நீக்கிக் கரனோடு தூடணன்ற னுயிரை வாங்கிச்
சிலைவணக்கி மான்மரிய வெய்தான் றன்னைத் தில்லைநகர்த் திருச்சித்ர கூடந் தன்னுள்
தலைவணக்கிக் கைகூப்பி யேத்த வல்லார் திரிதலால் தவமுடைத்தித் தரணி தானே
en: This earth is endowed with merit by the wanderings of those capable of praising
with folded hands and bent heads inside Tiruccitrakūṭam in the town of Tillai
the One, who, having killed Virādha with mountain[-like] large shoulders
that subdue [the foes’] power
received the striped bow that the great sage
of the generous Tamil [language] gave [Him]
removed the nose of the demoness whose eyes defeated the stag’s
took the life of Dūṣaṇa along with Khara’s
bent the bow [and] shot an arrow so that the deer died
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect

ta: தனமருவு வைதேகி பிரிய லுற்றுத் தளர்வெய்திச் சடாயுவைவை குந்தத் தேற்றி
வனமருவு கவியரசன் காதல் கொண்டு வாலியைக்கொன் றிலங்கைநக ரரக்கர் கோமான்
சினமடங்க மாருதியாற் சுடுவித் தானைத் தில்லைநகர்த் திருச்சித்ர கூடந் தன்னுள்
ளினிதமர்ந்த வம்மானை யிராமன் றன்னை யேத்துவா ரிணையடியே யேத்தி னேனே
en: I have praised the pair of feet of those who praise
Rāma, the Lord who is sweetly seated inside Tiruccitrakūṭam in the town of Tillai
who suffered separation from Vaidehī in whom wealth abides
lifted up Jaṭāyu to Vaikuṇṭha
felt affection for the king of the apes dwelling in the forest
killed Vālin
and had the city of Laṅkā burnt through Māruti
so that the anger of the emperor of the rakshasas was subdued
gloss: causative, participial noun, third person, masculine, singular, accusative
participial noun, imperfective aspect, third person, plural

ta: குரைகடலை யடலம்பான் மறுக வெய்து குலைகட்டி மறுகரையை யதனா லேறி
யெரிநெடுவே லரக்கரொடு மிலங்கை வேந்த னின்னுயிர்கொண் டவன்றம்பிக் கரசு மீந்து
திருமகளோ டினிதமர்ந்த செல்வன் றன்னைத் தில்லைநகர்த் திருச்சித்ர கூடந் தன்னுள்
ளரசமர்ந்தா னடிசூடு மரசை யல்லா லரசாக வெண்ணேன்மற் றரசு தானே
en: I shall not consider [any] other kingdom as a kingdom
other than the kingdom of adorning the feet of
Him who sat in governance inside Tiruccitrakūṭam in the town of Tillai
the Lord, who, having shot a victorious arrow so that the roaring sea whirled
built a bridge [across it], reached the other shore by means of that [bridge]
took the sweet life of the king of Laṅkā
along with [those] of the rakshasas with blazing long spears
gave the kingdom to his younger brother [and] sweetly sat with the auspicious Lady
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine, singular

ta: அம்பொனெடு மணிமாட வயோத்தி யெய்தி யரசெய்தி யகத்தியன்வாய்த் தான்முன் கொன்றான்
றன்பெருந்தொல் கதைகேட்டு மிதிலைச் செல்வி யுலகுய்யத் திருவயிறு வாய்த்த மக்கள்
செம்பவளத் திரள்வாய்த்தன் சரிதை கேட்டான் தில்லைநகர்த் திருச்சித்ர கூடந் தன்னுள்
ளெம்பெருமான் றன்சரிதை செவியாற் கண்ணாற் பருகுவோ மின்னமுத மதியோ மன்றே
en: We, who shall not value the sweet nectar, shall drink in with [our] eyes and ears the life story
of our Lord, is it not, inside Tiruccitrakūṭam in the town of Tillai
of the One, who, having reached Ayōdhyā with beautiful, tall, golden mansions [made of] gold
obtained the kingdom, listened from the mouth of Agastya to the great, old story of him
whom He had previously killed, [and]
listened to His [own] life story from the red coral[-like] round mouths of [His] children born
in the sacred womb of the daughter of Mithilā, so that the world is redeemed

ta: செறிதவச்சம் புகன்றனைச் சென்று கொன்று செழுமறையோ னுயிர்மீட்டு தவத்தோ னீந்த
நிறைமணிப்பூ ணணியுங்கொண் டிலவணன் றன்னைத் தம்பியால் வானேற்றி முனிவன் வேண்டத்
திறல்விளங்கு மிலக்குமனைப் பிரிந்தான் றன்னைத் தில்லைநகர்த் திருச்சித்ர கூடந் தன்னுள்
ளுறைவானை மறவாத வுள்ளந் தன்னை யுடையோம்மற் றுறுதுயர மடையோ மன்றே
en: We who possess a heart that does not forget
Him who lives inside Tiruccitrakūṭam in the town of Tillai
who, having gone [and] killed Śambuka of abundant tapas
recovered the life of the excellent brahmin
acquired wearable ornaments with splendid gems given by the sage
lifted up Lavaṇa to heaven by means of [His] younger brother
[and] became parted from Lakṣmaṇa shining with valour as the sage had requested
shall not suffer again from the grief that occurs, is it not [so]?

pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

ta: அன்றுசரா சரங்களைவை குந்தத் தேற்றி யடலரவப் பகையேறி யசுரர் தம்மை
வென்றிலங்கு மணிநெடுந்தோள் நான்குந் தோன்ற விண்முழுது மெதிர்வரத்தன் தாம மேவி
சென்றினிது வீற்றிருந்த வம்மான் றன்னைத் தில்லைநகர்த் திருச்சித்ர கூடந் தன்னுள்
ளென்றும்நின்றா னவனிவனென் றேத்தி நாளு மிறைஞ்சுமினோ யெப்பொழுதுந் தொண்டீர் நீரே
en: O you servants! Bow down [before Him] all the time, daily, and praise [by] saying
‘He is the One who stays forever inside Tiruccitrakūṭam in the town of Tillai
the Lord who, that day, having lifted up all living beings to Vaikuṇṭha
climbed on the enemy of murderous snakes, destroyed the asuras
[and] as four large arms with glittering gems appeared
and as the whole heaven came forward
reached His abode and went on to be blissfully enthroned [there].’
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

ta: தில்லைநகர்த் திருச்சித்ர கூடந் தன்னுள் திறல்விளங்கு மாருதியோ டமர்ந்தான் றன்னை
யெல்லையில்சீர்த் தயரதன்றன் மகனாய்த் தோன்றிற் றதுமுதலாத் தன்னுலகம் புக்க தீறாக்
கொல்லியலும் படைத்தானைக் கொற்ற வொள்வாள் கோழியர்கோன் குடைக்குலசே கரன்சொற் செய்த
நல்லியலின் றமிழ்மாலை பத்தும் வல்லார் நலந்திகழ்நா ரணனடிக்கீழ் நண்ணு வாரே
en: They shall arrive beneath the feet of Nārāyaṇa shining with goodness
those who master all ten [songs] of the garland in sweet Tamil of good quality
worded by Kulacēkaraṉ with the [royal] parasol, the king of the Kōḻi people
[who possesses] a victorious, glowing sword [and] an army with weapons given to killing
on Him who sat with Māruti shining with valour inside Tiruccitrakūṭam in the town of Tillai
the beginning being [His] appearing as the son of Daśaratha of limitless fame [and]
the end being His entering His world
gloss: participial noun, third person, masculine, singular
